statement: Mia writes a word in capital letters and holds it up to a mirror. Which word looks exactly the same in the mirror?

choices.misconception: I checked that M, A and T each look the same in a mirror, but forgot that the mirror also swaps their order, so it shows TAM.
I saw that BOB reads the same backwards, but forgot that the mirror also turns each B the wrong way round.
I checked that each letter of BOX can be folded top to bottom, but a mirror held in front of a word flips it left to right.
I knew S looks the same when it is turned upside down, so I thought it also looks the same in a mirror.

hints: Check two things: each letter, and the order of the letters.
A mirror swaps left and right. So every letter must look the same when flipped left to right, and the word must also read the same backwards. Test each word for both.
MAT turns into TAM. In BOB, BOX and SOS, the letters B and S face the wrong way. Now check the last word.

solutions.reliable: A mirror swaps left and right. That changes a word in two ways: each letter is flipped, and the order of the letters is reversed. MAT shows as TAM. In BOB, BOX and SOS, every B or S comes out facing the wrong way. In TOOT, the letters T and O look the same when flipped, and TOOT reads the same backwards, so the mirror shows TOOT. The idea to keep: a mirror flips the whole picture, so check the letters and their order.

whyOnTest: A mirror tests two kinds of matching at once: each letter must match its flip, and the word must read the same backwards.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
